newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds ended with modest gains on Wednesday evening amid light trading volume, with bonos failing to consolidate previous record highs, dealers said.

"We are tracking others. We showed a modest improvement in the 10-year spread over Bunds --to end at 65 basis points versus 67 basis points yesterday. Apart from that we are mimicking our German counterpart in light volume," a dealer said.
He stressed that the Italian debt market continued to outperform Spain, with the BTPs spread over Bonos trading at around 28 basis points versus 65 basis points one month ago.
"At this point I would sell Italy and buy Spain," a dealer in Madrid said. Although both countries have very good chances to enter in first EMU's wave, Italy's outlook is seen worse.
"This doesn't justify such a tiny spread," he said.
Despite a slight fall in Treasury one-year and 18-month bill yields earlier this morning, many analysts are ruling out any possible move in the key money market rate in the short run.
The focus is now on the June CPI announcement on Friday, with the market consensus forecasting a year-on-year increase at around 1.5/1.6 percent versus May's 1.5 percent.
"I don't expect the Bank of Spain change its rate," he said.
